name: Sheet-pan chicken fajitas
tip: Set everything in the middle of the table and let everyone build their own.
method: Heat oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Slice chicken and peppers into strips.
Toss chicken and peppers with oil, fajita seasoning, salt and pepper. Spread across the tray in a single layer so the edges roast golden.

Roast for 20–22 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through in the thickest part. Cut into the thickest piece: it should be steaming hot throughout with no pink meat, and the juices should run clear. If unsure, continue cooking.
Finish with lime off the heat, tasting in small additions.
Warm wraps and serve with grated cheddar and soured cream.

name: Crispy southern-style chicken burgers
tip: Crushed cornflakes give you a proper crunch without deep frying.
method: Heat oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Crush cornflakes and season with paprika.
Dip chicken in beaten egg, then press into the crumbs.

name: Creamy garlic parmesan chicken pasta
tip: A deep pan keeps washing-up to a minimum.
method: Cut the chicken into even 2 cm pieces, finely chop the garlic, grate the Parmesan and zest the lemon before starting. Prepare the listed chicken stock.
Heat the listed oil in a deep pan. Sauté the chicken for 4–5 minutes until lightly golden, then stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.

Add the penne and hot chicken stock. Simmer for the pasta packet time, stirring often and adding water in small splashes whenever the pasta is no longer mostly covered; the pasta should be nearly tender before adding the cream.

Stir in the cream and simmer gently until the pasta is tender, the sauce coats it and the chicken is fully cooked. Check the thickest chicken piece reaches 75°C for 30 seconds; continue cooking if needed.
Turn off the heat and stir through the measured Parmesan. Finish with lemon zest and a little juice, tasting as you go, then season and serve.

name: Slow-cooker BBQ pulled pork buns
tip: Start it in the morning and dinner practically takes care of itself.
method: Before switching on the slow cooker, pat the pork shoulder dry. Slice the onion and crush the garlic. Rub the whole joint with smoked paprika and garlic, then set it on the onion.

Add about 150 ml BBQ sauce and the apple cider vinegar around the 1.2 kg pork shoulder. Add 100 ml water if the cooker needs a little liquid; consult its instructions. Leave the whole joint intact while it slow-cooks.
Cook on low for 7–8 hours, until safely cooked and tender enough to pull apart easily with a fork.
Shred with two forks and stir through the cooking juices. If the sauce needs thickening, simmer it uncovered briefly before filling the buns.
Fill six brioche buns with shredded pork and divide the 300 g prepared coleslaw between them. Serve extra BBQ sauce only if separately purchased.

name: Beef & three-bean chilli
tip: Make extra and freeze portions for an easy future dinner.
method: Brown beef mince with diced onion and garlic. Drain excess fat if needed.
Add cumin, smoked paprika and chilli powder, then stir in one 400 g tin of chopped tomatoes and beans drained and rinsed from two 400 g tins (about 480 g drained in total).
Simmer gently for 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the mince is thoroughly cooked.
While the chilli simmers, cook 450 g dry rice (75 g per serving) following packet instructions. Measure this from the purchased 1 kg bag and keep the remaining dry rice for another meal.
Take the chilli off the heat and finish with lime in small additions. Serve over the cooked rice, with soured cream if desired.
ingredients: 450 g dry (buy 1 kg bag; keep the remainder)

name: Salt & pepper chicken stir-fry
tip: Prep everything first; a hot wok makes this a speedy dinner.
method: Slice chicken and toss with five-spice, a little cornflour, salt and pepper. Finely chop or grate the fresh ginger.
Prepare 250 g dried egg noodles following packet directions and drain.
Stir-fry the chicken in a hot pan with a little oil until golden and cooked through. Work in batches so it browns rather than steams.

Toss in the noodles, 2 tbsp soy sauce and 2 tbsp sweet chilli sauce. Cook the sauces through, then take off the heat and finish with lime in small additions. Serve hot.

name: Honey-soy salmon & greens
tip: A sweet-savoury glaze does all the heavy lifting.
method: Heat oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Finely grate the ginger and crush the garlic.
Whisk the ginger, garlic, honey, soy sauce and sesame oil together. Pat the salmon dry and place it with the broccoli on a lined tray.
Brush some glaze over the salmon and toss the broccoli with a spoonful. Keep the remaining glaze separate from the raw fish.

Bake for 12–18 minutes in total, depending on thickness. Brush on the reserved glaze for the final 2 minutes, watching closely so the honey does not burn. Check the salmon is opaque and flakes easily and the broccoli is tender.
Finish with lime juice off the heat. Serve the salmon and greens together; rice or potatoes are optional extra purchases, not included in this recipe’s ingredient estimate.

name: Sirloin steak & peppercorn sauce
tip: A restaurant-style plate without the restaurant bill.
method: Heat oven to 200°C. Cut potatoes into wedges, season and roast for 30–35 minutes. Crush the garlic and cut the butter into small pieces.
Pat steaks dry and season. Sear in a hot pan to your preferred doneness, turning as needed. Leave space between the steaks so they sear rather than steam.
Once the steaks have developed a dark golden crust, add the garlic and butter. Tilt the pan and spoon the foaming butter over the meat.
Rest steaks for at least 3 minutes. Check the outside is properly seared and follow appropriate guidance for the cut and diners; a food thermometer may help if available.
Warm peppercorn sauce and steam broccoli. Slice the rested steak, spoon over the garlicky pan juices and serve with the sauce, potatoes and broccoli.

name: Creamy Tuscan garlic salmon
tip: Sun-dried tomatoes bring big flavour to the creamy sauce.
method: Pat salmon dry, crush the two garlic cloves and chop the 60 g drained sun-dried tomatoes.
Sear the salmon in a pan with a little oil, skin-side down first if skin-on, then turn carefully.
Add the garlic, 150 g cherry tomatoes and sun-dried tomatoes; cook briefly until the tomatoes start to soften.
Pour in 150 ml double cream and simmer gently until the salmon is cooked through; check the thickest part following food-safety guidance rather than relying on browning alone.

steps: Peel the potatoes and cut into 2 cm chunks. Finely dice the onion and carrots, rinse the dried lentils and prepare the listed vegetable stock. Allow about 65 minutes overall; cook the potatoes alongside the lentil filling.

Heat the oil in a saucepan and soften the onion and carrots for 5 minutes. Add the lentils and measured stock, bring to a simmer and cook gently for about 25–30 minutes or the packet time, until the lentils are fully tender. Stir occasionally and add water if the pan dries out; uncover near the end so the filling is thick enough to hold its shape.

As soon as the lentils are simmering, put the potatoes in a separate pan of boiling water and cook for 15–20 minutes until tender. Drain well and mash, adding a little reserved potato cooking water if needed. Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) while the filling finishes cooking.

Spoon the hot lentil filling into an ovenproof dish, spread the mash over the top and roughen with a fork. Bake for about 20 minutes until the filling bubbles at the edges and the top is golden. Stand briefly before serving; older lentils may need extra simmering time.

name: Tomato butter bean stew
tip: A warming bowl of tomato butter bean stew with butter beans at its heart.
method: Drain and rinse the butter beans. Peel and finely dice the onion, mince the garlic, finely chop the parsley and wash the spinach.
Warm 1 tbsp oil in a deep pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5–6 minutes until softened, then stir in the garlic and parsley for 30 seconds without browning.
Pour in the chopped tomatoes and simmer for 5 minutes. Stir in the butter beans and simmer uncovered for another 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally.

name: Classic banana bread
tip: A proper two-pound loaf: spotty bananas make the best slices.
method: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Grease and line a 900 g/2 lb loaf tin with baking parchment.
Mash the peeled bananas in a large bowl. Melt the butter and let it cool slightly.
Whisk the eggs, sugar, melted butter and vanilla into the mashed banana.
Fold in the self-raising flour, baking powder and cinnamon just until no dry flour remains; do not overmix.
Spoon into the lined tin and bake for 55–65 minutes. A skewer inserted in the centre should come out without wet batter. Cover loosely with foil if browning too quickly.
Cool in the tin for 15 minutes, then move to a rack for at least 10 minutes before slicing. Store covered and eat within a sensible food-safe period.

name: Soft cinnamon swirl rolls
tip: A cosy weekend bake: allow time for two rises.
method: Warm the milk until lukewarm, not hot. Mix the flour, yeast, caster sugar and a pinch of salt. Add the milk, egg and 50 g softened butter and knead for 8–10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and leave in a warm place for about 60 minutes or until doubled in size.
Mix 30 g soft butter with the brown sugar and cinnamon. Roll the dough to roughly 35 × 25 cm, spread with the filling and roll up tightly from the long edge.
Cut into nine equal spirals and arrange slightly apart in a lined baking tin. Cover and rise for 35–45 minutes until visibly puffy.
Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Bake for 22–27 minutes until golden and cooked through in the centres.
Cool for 10 minutes. Stir the icing sugar with 1–2 tsp water and drizzle over the warm rolls.

name: Beef in black bean sauce with rice
cost_basis: Actual BasketBoss source-aware meal adapter using existing guide packs and the isolated catalogue-700 indicative pack overlay. Pantry ingredients use the existing policy; Shop prices packs actually purchased. Estimates are unverified.
tip: A very hot pan and small batches brown the beef instead of stewing it.
ingredients: 600 g, cut across the grain into thin strips
method: Put the rinsed rice in a saucepan with 450 ml tap water. Bring to the boil, cover and simmer on low for 12 minutes, then turn off and leave covered for 10 minutes.

Toss the beef with the soy sauce and cornflour. Heat half the oil in a large frying pan or wok until hot. Fry the beef in two uncrowded batches for 1–2 minutes each until browned; transfer to a clean plate.
Add the remaining oil, onion and peppers to the pan. Stir-fry for 4–5 minutes until lightly coloured but still crisp. Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 30 seconds.

Add the black bean sauce and 60 ml tap water. Simmer for 2 minutes, then return the beef and any juices. Toss for 1–2 minutes until the beef is hot throughout and the sauce clings to it; avoid prolonged boiling that toughens the strips.
Fluff the rice and divide between four bowls. Spoon over the beef, peppers and sauce. The listed rice is the complete accompaniment.

name: Sesame prawn toast with cucumber salad
cost_basis: Actual BasketBoss source-aware meal adapter using existing guide packs and the isolated catalogue-700 indicative pack overlay. Pantry ingredients use the existing policy; Shop prices packs actually purchased. Estimates are unverified.
tip: Keep the topping thin and even so the prawns cook before the sesame burns.
ingredients: 300 g, thawed if frozen and patted dry, peeled and deveined
method: Mix the vinegar and sugar until dissolved, then toss with the sliced cucumber and refrigerate while making the toast.

Pulse or finely chop the prawns with the egg white, soy sauce and ginger into a spreadable paste. Keep it chilled until needed. Spread evenly over the bread, reaching the edges, and press the prawn side firmly into the sesame seeds. Cut each slice into four triangles.

Pour the oil into a deep-sided frying pan to make a shallow layer; never fill the pan more than one third. Heat to about 170°C. Keep water away from the hot oil and have a lid nearby; do not leave the pan unattended.

Fry the triangles in small batches, prawn side down first, for about 2–3 minutes, then turn and cook the bread side for 1 minute. The coating should be golden and the prawn centre opaque and cooked through; check the thickest topping reaches 75°C for 30 seconds. Lower the heat if the sesame browns too quickly.
Drain briefly on kitchen paper and serve at once with the cucumber salad, four triangles per person as a starter. Let the frying oil cool completely before disposal.

name: Chicken jalfrezi with pilau rice
cost_basis: Actual BasketBoss source-aware meal adapter using existing guide packs and the isolated catalogue-700 indicative pack overlay. Pantry ingredients use the existing policy; Shop prices packs actually purchased. Estimates are unverified.
tip: Cook the peppers until coloured before adding tomatoes for a brighter jalfrezi flavour.
ingredients: 4 g, divided between curry and rice
method: Heat 20 ml oil in a large pan. Cook the onion and peppers for 7–8 minutes until softened with a little colour. Stir in garlic, ginger, chilli, 5 g cumin, coriander and 3 g turmeric for 1 minute.

Add the chicken and turn through the spices for 3–4 minutes. Pour in the tomatoes and 150 ml tap water, bring to a gentle simmer and cook uncovered for 18–22 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and the chicken reaches 75°C for 30 seconds.

Meanwhile, warm the remaining 10 ml oil in a saucepan. Stir in the remaining 2 g cumin and 2 g turmeric for 20 seconds, then add the rinsed rice, half the salt and 450 ml tap water. Cover and simmer on low for 12 minutes, then rest off the heat for 10 minutes.
Stir the garam masala and remaining salt into the curry. If needed, simmer for a few more minutes to reduce the sauce; the peppers should still have some shape.
Fluff the pilau with a fork and divide between four bowls with the chicken jalfrezi.

cost_basis: Actual BasketBoss source-aware meal adapter using existing guide packs and the isolated catalogue-700 indicative pack overlay. Pantry ingredients use the existing policy; Shop prices packs actually purchased. Estimates are unverified.
tip: Dry grated onion and a short chill help the kebabs stay on their skewers.
ingredients: 1 small onion, grated and squeezed dry
method: Mix the lamb mince with the squeezed grated onion, two crushed garlic cloves, ginger, ground spices, chopped coriander and salt. Knead with clean hands for 1–2 minutes until tacky. Divide into eight portions and shape firmly around metal skewers into short, even kebabs. Refrigerate for 20 minutes.
Mix the yoghurt with the remaining garlic, mint and juice from half the lemon. Cover and keep chilled. Slice the cucumber and cut the remaining lemon half into wedges.

Warm the pittas under the grill briefly, keeping them away from raw-meat juices. Serve two kebabs per person with one pitta, cucumber and mint yoghurt.

cost_basis: Actual BasketBoss source-aware meal adapter using existing guide packs and the isolated catalogue-700 indicative pack overlay. Pantry ingredients use the existing policy; Shop prices packs actually purchased. Estimates are unverified.
tip: Flattening the chicken helps breast and legs finish together; thermometer checks decide doneness.
method: Mix the chilli, garlic, lemon juice, 6 g paprika, oregano, vinegar, 20 ml oil and 3 g salt. Rub over the flattened chicken, including under the skin where possible. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes. Keep all raw chicken and marinade separate from serving utensils.

Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Put the chicken skin-side up on a roasting tray and roast for 55–65 minutes, lowering the oven slightly if the skin colours too quickly. Check both the thickest thigh and breast reach 75°C for 30 seconds, without touching bone. Rest for 10 minutes before carving.

For the rice, heat the remaining 10 ml oil in a saucepan and cook the onion and pepper for 6 minutes. Stir in the remaining 2 g paprika, turmeric, rinsed rice and 2 g salt. Add 500 ml tap water, cover and simmer on low for 12 minutes.
Scatter the frozen peas over the rice, replace the lid and cook for 3 minutes, then leave off the heat for 5 minutes. Check the peas are piping hot and fluff the rice.
Carve the rested chicken into four portions and serve over the spicy rice. Do not use raw leftover marinade as a serving sauce.

Heat a heavy frying pan over medium-high heat and brush lightly with oil. Toast the cut sides of the buns and set aside. Work in batches so there is room to smash each patty.

Place two mince balls in the hot pan and immediately press very thin with a sturdy spatula, using a piece of baking paper between spatula and beef if needed. Season with salt and pepper. Cook without moving for 2–3 minutes until well browned.

name: Battered haddock and chips with mushy peas
cost_basis: Actual BasketBoss source-aware meal adapter using existing guide packs and the isolated catalogue-700 indicative pack overlay. Pantry ingredients use the existing policy; Shop prices packs actually purchased. Estimates are unverified.
tip: Cold batter and hot oil give a crisp coat; dry fish prevents it sliding off.
ingredients: 4 skinless, boneless fillets, about 600 g total
method: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Parboil the chips in tap water for 5 minutes, drain and steam-dry for 5 minutes. Toss with 30 ml oil and some salt on a large tray. Roast for 30–35 minutes, turning once, until golden.
Cook the peas in boiling water for 3 minutes, drain and mash with butter, pepper and a pinch of the measured salt. Keep warm.

Heat the frying oil in a large deep saucepan to 180°C, keeping it no more than one third full. Never leave it unattended or add water. Mix 150 g flour, cornflour, baking powder and a little salt, then whisk in the cold sparkling water just until a light batter forms.

ingredients: 1.6 kg raw bone-in pork spare ribs
method: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Put the ribs in a deep roasting tin. Mix the smoked paprika, crushed garlic, brown sugar, salt, half the pepper and 10 ml vinegar into a paste and rub all over the ribs. Cover the tin tightly with foil; no added water or cooking oil is required.

Roast covered for 2 hours 30 minutes until very tender and the meat yields easily when pierced between the bones. Check the thickest part is cooked through and reaches 75°C for 30 seconds, keeping the probe away from bone. If still firm, cover again and cook longer before glazing.

Meanwhile, slice the cabbage very finely, grate the carrots and finely slice the half onion. Mix the mayonnaise with the remaining 10 ml vinegar and pepper, then toss with all the prepared vegetables. Cover and refrigerate until serving.

Lift the ribs onto a clean roasting tray and carefully pour away the accumulated cooking liquid and rendered fat. Turn the oven up to 220°C (200°C fan). Brush the tender ribs with all the measured BBQ sauce.

Roast uncovered for 15–20 minutes, turning once and brushing with the sauce on the tray, until sticky and caramelised. Watch the glaze closely so the sugar colours without burning. Keep the ribs out of direct flame; this recipe is oven cooked.
Rest for 10 minutes, cut between the bones and divide into four portions. Serve with the chilled cabbage, carrot and onion slaw.

method: Bring a large pan of water to the boil. Cook the egg noodles following the packet timing, leaving them just firm. Drain, rinse briefly under cold water and shake very dry; separate any clumps with your fingers.
Mix the soy sauce, sesame oil and grated ginger in a small bowl. Slice the chicken into thin even strips, keeping the raw meat and its board away from the cooked noodles and vegetables.

Heat a large wok until very hot. Add half the cooking oil and stir-fry half the chicken for 3–4 minutes, turning constantly. Repeat with the remaining oil and chicken. Check the thickest chicken reaches 75°C for 30 seconds, then lift it onto a clean plate.
Put the carrot and garlic in the hot wok and stir-fry for 2 minutes. Add the bean sprouts and spring onions and cook for 2 minutes more until the sprouts are steaming hot throughout.

Return the chicken, add the drained noodles and pour over the prepared sauce. Toss over a high heat for 2–3 minutes until everything is hot and evenly coated. Divide between four bowls and serve immediately.

method: Put the chicken stock and grated ginger in a large saucepan and bring to a gentle simmer. Add the chicken breasts and poach gently for 12–15 minutes, turning once, until the thickest part reaches 75°C for 30 seconds.
Lift the chicken onto a clean board. Leave for 2 minutes until safe to handle, then shred finely using two forks. Keep the simmering stock on the hob.
Mash half the sweetcorn roughly with a fork, leaving the rest whole. Add both to the stock with the soy sauce and simmer for 3–4 minutes; frozen kernels must be piping hot.

name: Char siu pork with rice
cost_basis: Actual BasketBoss source-aware meal adapter using existing guide packs and the isolated catalogue-700 indicative pack overlay. Pantry ingredients use the existing policy; Shop prices packs actually purchased. Estimates are unverified.
tip: Allow two hours for marinating. Keep a clean portion of sauce aside before it touches raw pork, then use only that portion for glazing.
method: Mix the hoisin, soy sauce, 30 ml of the honey, vinegar, five-spice, ginger and garlic. Put 2 tablespoons of this clean mixture in a covered bowl in the fridge for glazing. Coat the pork strips in the remaining marinade, cover and refrigerate for 2 hours.
Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Line a deep roasting tin with foil, add 150 ml tap water beneath a rack and place the pork strips on the rack. Discard the marinade that touched raw pork.
Roast for 55–65 minutes, turning after 30 minutes. If the drips begin to burn, add a little more hot tap water to the bottom of the tin. Check the thickest pork reaches at least 75°C for 30 seconds.

Mix the clean reserved marinade with the remaining 15 ml honey. Brush over the pork and roast for another 5 minutes until glossy and lightly charred at the edges. Rest the cooked pork on a clean board for 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, cook the rice with 600 ml tap water, covered over a low heat for 12–15 minutes or according to its packet, then rest covered for 5 minutes. Heat a large frying pan, brush the pak choi with the listed oil and sear cut-side down for 2 minutes; add 60 ml tap water, cover and steam for 3–4 minutes until tender.

Slice the rested pork across the grain into thin pieces. Divide the rice and pak choi between four plates and lay the glossy pork over the rice. Use only cooked tray juices or clean glaze for serving, never uncooked marinade.

tip: The two-hour marinade is included in the time. Vindaloo is hot and tangy; reduce the chilli powder before cooking for a gentler household version.
method: Mix the vinegar, crushed garlic, grated ginger, chilli powder, cumin, coriander, turmeric and cinnamon in a non-metallic bowl. Add the lamb, turn to coat, cover and refrigerate for 2 hours.
Heat the cooking oil in a heavy lidded casserole. Fry the chopped onions over a medium heat for 10 minutes until golden and soft, stirring so they do not catch.
Add the marinated lamb and all its marinade. Cook, stirring, for 5 minutes. Add the chopped tomatoes, salt and 250 ml tap water. Bring just to the boil, then cover and reduce to a low simmer.

Cook gently for 90 minutes, stirring every 20 minutes and adding a small splash of hot tap water only if the pan becomes dry. The lamb should be fork-tender and fully cooked; simmer uncovered for the final 10 minutes if the sauce needs to thicken.

During the final 20 minutes, cook the rinsed rice in 600 ml tap water for 12–15 minutes, covered, or according to packet instructions. Rest off the heat for 5 minutes. Divide the rice and the hot tangy lamb curry between four plates.

name: Lahmacun with chopped salad
cost_basis: Actual BasketBoss source-aware meal adapter using existing guide packs and the isolated catalogue-700 indicative pack overlay. Pantry ingredients use the existing policy; Shop prices packs actually purchased. Estimates are unverified.
tip: Spread a very thin raw meat layer right to the edge. A thick topping stays wet and prevents the flatbread from crisping.
method: Mix 380 g of the flour with the yeast and 4 g salt. Add 240 ml lukewarm tap water and 10 ml olive oil, then knead for 8–10 minutes until smooth. Cover and leave in a warm place for about 1 hour until doubled.

Mix the raw beef with the finely chopped onion, two finely chopped tomatoes, pepper, paprika, cumin, half the parsley, the remaining oil and 2 g salt. Stir and press with a spoon into a finely textured spreadable mixture.
Heat the oven to 240°C (220°C fan) with two baking trays inside. Divide the dough into four pieces. Using the reserved flour, roll each piece very thinly into a 24 cm round on baking paper.

Spread one-quarter of the meat mixture very thinly over each round, leaving only a tiny rim. Transfer carefully to the hot trays. Bake two at a time for 10–12 minutes until the edges are crisp and the meat is fully cooked, reaching 75°C for 30 seconds. Repeat with the remaining two.
Toss the remaining sliced tomato, cucumber and parsley together. Serve each hot lahmacun with salad and a lemon wedge; squeeze the lemon over and roll loosely to eat.

name: Beef birria quesatacos
cost_basis: Actual BasketBoss source-aware meal adapter using existing guide packs and the isolated catalogue-700 indicative pack overlay. Pantry ingredients use the existing policy; Shop prices packs actually purchased. Estimates are unverified.
tip: This supermarket version uses ordinary chilli powder and smoked paprika. Chill leftover braising broth promptly; never leave cooked meat or broth at room temperature overnight.
method: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Reserve half an onion, finely diced, in a covered bowl in the fridge for serving. Quarter the remaining one and a half onions. Heat 15 ml of the oil in a heavy lidded casserole and brown the beef in two batches for about 8 minutes total. Add only the quartered onions and garlic and cook for 2 minutes.

Add the tomatoes, beef stock, chilli powder, smoked paprika, cumin, oregano and vinegar. Bring to a simmer, cover tightly and place in the oven for about 3 hours until the beef falls apart easily. Check halfway and add hot tap water only if needed to keep the meat mostly covered.

Lift the cooked beef into a bowl and shred with two forks. Blend the onion, tomatoes and garlic into the broth using a stick blender, keeping the blade submerged to prevent hot splashes. Simmer for 5–10 minutes to concentrate; skim off a little of the reddish surface fat into a small bowl.

Mix the shredded beef with 3 tablespoons of the broth. Heat a large non-stick frying pan over a medium heat and brush with some of the remaining 10 ml oil. Dip the outside of one tortilla briefly into the surface of the hot broth and lay it in the pan.

Fill half the tortilla with beef and mozzarella, then fold over. Fry for 1–2 minutes on each side until crisp and the cheese melts. Repeat in batches with all 12 tortillas, using the remaining oil sparingly.
Serve three quesatacos per person with the reserved finely diced half onion, chopped coriander and lime wedges. Ladle the remaining piping-hot broth into four small bowls for dipping.

Add the tomatoes, beef stock, chilli powder, smoked paprika, cumin, oregano and vinegar. Bring to a simmer, cover tightly and place in the oven for about 3 hours until the beef falls apart easily. Check halfway and add hot tap water only if needed to keep the meat mostly covered.

Lift the cooked beef into a bowl and shred with two forks. Blend the onion, tomatoes and garlic into the broth using a stick blender, keeping the blade submerged to prevent hot splashes. Simmer for 5–10 minutes to concentrate; skim off a little of the reddish surface fat into a small bowl.

Mix the shredded beef with 3 tablespoons of the broth. Heat a large non-stick frying pan over a medium heat and brush with some of the remaining 10 ml oil. Dip the outside of one tortilla briefly into the surface of the hot broth and lay it in the pan.

Fill half the tortilla with beef and mozzarella, then fold over. Fry for 1–2 minutes on each side until crisp and the cheese melts. Repeat in batches with all 12 tortillas, using the remaining oil sparingly.
Serve three quesatacos per person with the reserved finely diced half onion, chopped coriander and lime wedges. Ladle the remaining piping-hot broth into four small bowls for dipping.

name: Beef Wellington with red wine gravy
category: Date Nights · Special meals for two
cost_basis: Actual BasketBoss source-aware meal adapter using existing guide packs and the isolated catalogue-700 indicative pack overlay. Pantry ingredients use the existing policy; Shop prices packs actually purchased. Estimates are unverified.
tip: Both the beef and mushroom filling must cool before wrapping. The total time includes two chilling periods; a thermometer is more reliable than pastry colour.
method: Pat the beef dry and season with half the salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a frying pan and sear the beef on all sides for 5–6 minutes. Brush with the mustard and cool on a clean plate. Fry the finely chopped mushrooms in 15 g butter with the remaining seasoning for 12–15 minutes until very dry. Spread on a plate and cool fully.

Overlap the prosciutto on a large sheet of food-safe cling film. Spread the cold mushroom mixture evenly over it, sit the cooled beef at one end and roll into a snug parcel using the film. Twist the ends and refrigerate for 30 minutes, then remove and discard the film.

Unroll the cold pastry. Put the beef parcel on it, brush the joining edges with beaten egg and wrap tightly, trimming only excess overlapping pastry. Seal the underside and ends. Put seam-side down on baking paper on a tray. Brush with egg, use any pastry trimmings for simple decorations and chill for another 30 minutes.

Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Brush with the remaining egg and make two small steam holes. Bake for 35–40 minutes until deep golden. Check the centre with a clean thermometer: 60–65°C gives a pink whole-muscle fillet after resting; for diners needing fully cooked beef, continue to 75°C and shield the pastry if necessary. Rest for 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, melt the remaining 10 g butter in a small saucepan. Soften the shallots for 4 minutes, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then add the red wine. Simmer for 3 minutes before gradually whisking in the stock. Simmer for 8–10 minutes until lightly thickened.
Cut the rested Wellington into four thick slices with a serrated knife. Serve the red-wine gravy beside it rather than soaking the pastry.

name: Poached salmon with hollandaise and new potatoes
category: Date Nights · Special meals for two
cost_basis: Actual BasketBoss source-aware meal adapter using existing guide packs and the isolated catalogue-700 indicative pack overlay. Pantry ingredients use the existing policy; Shop prices packs actually purchased. Estimates are unverified.
tip: Use pasteurised egg yolks for diners at higher risk. Keep the sauce warm over barely warm water and serve immediately; it must never boil.
method: Halve the lemon. Squeeze and reserve the juice from one half for the hollandaise, then slice the other half for poaching. Put the potatoes in a saucepan, cover with tap water and add 2 g salt. Bring to the boil and simmer for 15–20 minutes until tender, then drain and keep warm.

Fill a shallow pan with enough tap water to cover the salmon. Add the lemon slices and dill stalks, bring to a bare simmer and lower in the salmon. Poach gently for 8–10 minutes, keeping the water below a rolling boil, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily; the centre should reach 63°C.

Meanwhile, melt the butter in a small pan. Put the egg yolks, 1 tablespoon lemon juice and 1 tablespoon cold tap water in a heatproof bowl over a pan of barely simmering water, with the bowl clear of the water.

Whisk continuously for 3–4 minutes until the yolks thicken slightly. Remove the bowl from the heat and whisk in the warm melted butter very slowly, a little at a time, to make a thick pouring sauce. Add the remaining salt and pepper. If too thick, whisk in a teaspoon of warm tap water.

Lift the salmon out carefully and let excess water drain off. Serve with the hot potatoes and freshly made hollandaise, finishing with the listed dill fronds. Serve immediately and discard sauce left at room temperature; do not keep it warm for prolonged periods.

tip: Ask for the tough outer membrane to be removed from the monkfish. Wrap snugly, and use a thermometer to avoid drying out the firm fish.

method: Heat the grill to high and line the grill pan with foil. Pat the cleaned sardines completely dry, brush with 15 ml olive oil and season inside and out with 2 g salt.

tip: Canned beans make this practical without an overnight soak. Drain all four listed tins and keep enough sauce in the pot during the long bake. The pantry ledger records the labelled net tin weight, while the edible drained yield is about 960 g.
method: Heat the oven to 170°C (150°C fan). Fry the bacon in a heavy lidded ovenproof casserole over a medium heat for 5 minutes until it releases fat. Add the onions and cook for 8 minutes until softened.

Stir in all the drained beans from the four tins, passata, treacle, maple syrup, mustard, vinegar, 2 g salt and 300 ml tap water. Bring to a simmer, cover and bake for 75 minutes, stirring halfway. Add a splash of hot tap water if the sauce becomes dry.

For the cornbread, grease a 20 cm square tin with 5 g of the butter. Mix the cornmeal, flour, baking powder and remaining salt in a bowl. Whisk the milk, eggs and remaining 45 g melted butter, then stir into the dry ingredients just until combined.

After the beans have baked for 75 minutes, turn the oven up to 200°C (180°C fan). Remove the casserole lid and put the cornbread tin alongside it. Bake both for 25–30 minutes until the beans are thick and glossy and the cornbread is risen, golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Rest the cornbread for 10 minutes, then cut into eight squares. Divide the hot beans between four bowls and serve with two cornbread squares each.

tip: Blend the soup carefully with the blade kept submerged. Cook the toasties over a moderate heat so the cheese melts before the bread burns.
method: Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan. Soften the onion and carrot for 8 minutes over a medium-low heat, stirring occasionally. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, vegetable stock, salt and pepper. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 20 minutes until the carrot is completely soft.
Take the pan off the heat, add the basil and blend carefully until smooth using a stick blender with its blade submerged. Stir in the cream and return to a low heat until hot, without boiling hard.

Butter one side of each bread slice. Make four sandwiches with the grated Cheddar inside and the buttered sides facing out. Put in a large frying pan over a medium-low heat and cook in batches for 3–4 minutes per side until crisp and golden and the cheese is melted.
Cut the toasties in half and serve each person a bowl of hot tomato soup with one cheese toastie. Keep the soup warm gently while finishing the sandwiches.

name: Bacon and cabbage with parsley sauce
cost_basis: Actual BasketBoss source-aware meal adapter using existing guide packs and the isolated catalogue-700 indicative pack overlay. Pantry ingredients use the existing policy; Shop prices packs actually purchased. Estimates are unverified.
tip: Check the gammon packet for soaking or cooking guidance. Use fresh water if the cooking liquor tastes very salty; do not automatically add more salt.
method: Follow any soaking instructions on the gammon packet. Put the joint in a large pot and cover with fresh cold tap water. Bring slowly to a simmer, skim away surface foam and cook gently for about 80–90 minutes, or according to the packet weight guidance, until the thickest part reaches 75°C for 30 seconds.

During the final 25 minutes, boil the potatoes in a separate pan of tap water for 18–20 minutes until tender. Add the cabbage wedges to the gammon pot for the final 12–15 minutes if the liquor is not too salty; otherwise cook them in fresh water.

For the sauce, melt the butter in a small saucepan, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the warm milk, keeping the mixture smooth. Simmer gently for 4–5 minutes until thickened.
Take the sauce off the heat and stir in the chopped parsley and black pepper. Keep warm gently without prolonged boiling.

Lift the gammon out and rest for 10 minutes before slicing. Serve with the drained potatoes, tender cabbage and parsley sauce. Cool any remaining cooked gammon promptly and refrigerate within 2 hours.

name: Lamb moussaka
cost_basis: Actual BasketBoss source-aware meal adapter using existing guide packs and the isolated catalogue-700 indicative pack overlay. Pantry ingredients use the existing policy; Shop prices packs actually purchased. Estimates are unverified.
tip: Roast the aubergine rather than frying it in excess oil. Rest the finished bake for 15 minutes so the layers slice more cleanly.
method: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Brush the aubergine and potato slices with 30 ml olive oil, season with half the salt and spread over two trays. Roast for 20–25 minutes until tender and lightly golden, turning once.

Meanwhile, heat the remaining oil in a saucepan. Soften the onion for 5 minutes, add the lamb and brown for 7–8 minutes, breaking it into small pieces. Add the garlic, cinnamon and oregano for 1 minute, then the tomatoes, remaining salt and pepper. Simmer for 15 minutes until thick.

Melt the butter in a second pan, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the warm milk and simmer for 4–5 minutes until thick and smooth. Take off the heat, cool for 5 minutes, then whisk in the beaten egg and half the Parmesan.

Reduce the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Layer the potatoes in a deep baking dish, then half the aubergines, the thick lamb sauce and the remaining aubergines. Spread the béchamel on top and scatter over the remaining Parmesan.
Bake for 35–40 minutes until the top is golden and the centre reaches 75°C for 30 seconds. Rest for 15 minutes before cutting into four generous portions.

name: American pot-roast beef with carrots
cost_basis: Actual BasketBoss source-aware meal adapter using existing guide packs and the isolated catalogue-700 indicative pack overlay. Pantry ingredients use the existing policy; Shop prices packs actually purchased. Estimates are unverified.
tip: Use a whole braising cut such as brisket, not a quick-cooking steak. Keep the casserole covered and cook until fork-tender before slicing.
method: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Pat the brisket dry and season with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a large lidded casserole and brown the joint on all sides for 8–10 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
Add the onions and celery to the pan and cook for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and flour and stir for 1 minute, then gradually stir in the beef stock and Worcestershire sauce, scraping the base.
Return the whole beef joint with the thyme. The liquid should come about halfway up the meat; add a little hot tap water if needed. Bring to a simmer, cover tightly and cook in the oven for 2 hours.

Turn the beef carefully, add the carrots and potatoes around it and cover again. Cook for another 60–75 minutes until the joint is very tender and the vegetables are cooked through. Add a little hot water only if the pan looks dry.
Lift the beef onto a clean board and rest for 15 minutes, loosely covered. Remove thyme stems. If the gravy is thin, simmer the casserole uncovered on the hob for 5–10 minutes.
Slice the brisket across the grain. Serve with the carrots, potatoes and onion gravy. Cool any leftovers promptly and refrigerate within 2 hours.

name: Homemade English breakfast muffins
cost_basis: Actual BasketBoss source-aware meal adapter using existing guide packs and the isolated catalogue-700 indicative pack overlay. Pantry ingredients use the existing policy; Shop prices packs actually purchased. Estimates are unverified.
tip: English muffins cook on a low griddle rather than in muffin tins. Split with a fork after cooling to reveal their rough open crumb.
method: Mix 425 g flour with the yeast, sugar and salt. Add the lukewarm milk, 75 ml lukewarm tap water and 25 g melted butter. Knead for 8–10 minutes using the reserved flour only as needed until smooth and elastic.
Put the dough in a bowl, cover and leave in a warm place for about 1 hour until doubled. Gently flatten to 2 cm thick, then cut eight rounds with an 8 cm cutter, rerolling scraps once.
Dust a tray with half the cornmeal. Put the rounds on it, sprinkle with the remaining cornmeal, cover loosely and leave for 30 minutes until slightly puffed.

Heat a heavy frying pan over a low heat. Cook the muffins in two batches for 7–8 minutes on each side, turning carefully, until browned and cooked in the centre. Reduce the heat if the outside browns too quickly; the centre should reach about 94°C for a fully baked bread crumb.

Cool on a rack for at least 10 minutes, then split with a fork. Toast the cut sides if desired and share the reserved 10 g butter between them. Makes eight muffins: two per person. Freeze spare cooled muffins on the day they are made.

name: Cinnamon-raisin breakfast loaf
cost_basis: Actual BasketBoss source-aware meal adapter using existing guide packs and the isolated catalogue-700 indicative pack overlay. Pantry ingredients use the existing policy; Shop prices packs actually purchased. Estimates are unverified.
tip: Cool before slicing so the swirl sets. The recipe makes eight substantial slices, two per person; freeze spare slices for quick toast later.
method: Mix 430 g flour, the yeast, 30 g sugar and salt. Add 250 ml lukewarm milk, the beaten egg and 40 g melted butter. Knead for 8–10 minutes, using the reserved flour sparingly, until smooth. Cover and leave for 90 minutes or until doubled.
Grease a 900 g loaf tin lightly using a little of the soft filling butter. Mix the remaining 40 g sugar with the cinnamon. Roll the risen dough into a rectangle roughly 25 × 35 cm.
Spread the remaining soft butter over the dough, scatter with cinnamon sugar and raisins and roll tightly from the short end. Pinch the seam closed and put seam-side down in the tin.

Cover loosely and leave for 45 minutes until well risen. Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan), brush the loaf with the reserved 20 ml milk and bake for 30–35 minutes until deep golden and the centre reaches about 94°C. Cover loosely with foil if the top darkens too quickly.
Turn onto a rack and cool for at least 30 minutes before cutting into eight slices. Serve two slices per person; the cooled loaf can be sliced and frozen on the day of baking.

name: Grilled kippers with lemon butter and toast
cost_basis: Actual BasketBoss source-aware meal adapter using existing guide packs and the isolated catalogue-700 indicative pack overlay. Pantry ingredients use the existing policy; Shop prices packs actually purchased. Estimates are unverified.
tip: Kippers contain fine bones. Choose responsibly prepared kippers and follow the pack’s cooking guidance; hot fish must be checked carefully before eating.
method: Heat the grill to medium and line a grill pan with foil. Lay the split kippers skin-side down on the rack and dot with 30 g of the butter.

Grill for 6–10 minutes, following the packet guidance if longer, until the fish is piping hot throughout and the edges are lightly golden. The thickest fish should reach 63°C; do not rely on the smoked colour alone.
Meanwhile, toast the bread and share the remaining 10 g butter between the slices. Cut the lemon into wedges.

Divide the cooked kippers into four portions and serve one portion with toast and a lemon wedge per person, adding the listed black pepper. Remind diners to remove the central backbone and watch carefully for fine bones.

name: Toasted fruit teacakes
cost_basis: Actual BasketBoss source-aware meal adapter using existing guide packs and the isolated catalogue-700 indicative pack overlay. Pantry ingredients use the existing policy; Shop prices packs actually purchased. Estimates are unverified.
tip: These are fruit bread buns, not cake. Cool before splitting, then toast gently; dried fruit catches quickly under a hot grill.
method: Mix 430 g flour with the yeast, sugar and salt. Add 260 ml lukewarm milk and 40 g soft butter. Knead for 8–10 minutes, using the reserved flour sparingly, until smooth and elastic.
Knead in the currants until evenly distributed. Cover the dough in a bowl and leave in a warm place for about 1 hour until doubled.
Divide into eight pieces, shape into smooth flat buns about 9 cm wide and put on a baking-paper-lined tray. Cover loosely and leave for 40 minutes until noticeably puffed.

Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Brush with the remaining 20 ml milk and bake for 18–22 minutes until golden and cooked through; the centres should reach about 94°C. Cool on a rack for at least 30 minutes.

Split the teacakes horizontally and toast the cut faces gently until golden, watching the currants closely. Share the remaining 30 g butter between them. Makes eight teacakes, two per person; freeze spare cooled buns on the day of baking.

name: Chicken madras with rice
cost_basis: Actual BasketBoss source-aware meal adapter using existing guide packs and the isolated catalogue-700 indicative pack overlay. Pantry ingredients use the existing policy; Shop prices packs actually purchased. Estimates are unverified.
tip: Bloom the spices briefly in the onion oil, then add liquid before they scorch. This is a hot curry; use a milder recipe for chilli-sensitive eaters.
method: Heat the oil in a heavy saucepan over a medium-low heat. Add the finely chopped onions and half the salt. Cook for 12–15 minutes, stirring often, until soft and golden rather than deeply browned.

Add the crushed garlic and grated ginger and stir for 1 minute. Add the cumin, coriander, turmeric and chilli powder. Stir for 30 seconds, then immediately pour in the passata and 150 ml tap water so the spices cannot burn.
Stir in the tamarind paste. Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce darkens and thickens. Add the chicken pieces and turn them through the sauce.

Cover loosely and simmer gently for 15–18 minutes, stirring twice, until every chicken piece is cooked through. The thickest piece must reach 75°C for 30 seconds; continue cooking if necessary. Add a little tap water only if the sauce catches.

Meanwhile, put the drained rice in a separate saucepan with 450 ml tap water and the remaining salt. Bring to the boil, cover, reduce to the lowest heat and cook for 12 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave covered for 8 minutes; this fits inside the curry cooking time.

Fluff the rice and divide between four plates. Spoon the chicken and hot tomato-tamarind sauce alongside. Cool any leftovers promptly and refrigerate within 2 hours; cool rice within 1 hour, refrigerate and use within 24 hours. Reheat once until steaming throughout.

name: Paneer tikka skewers with mint chutney
cost_basis: Actual BasketBoss source-aware meal adapter using existing guide packs and the isolated catalogue-700 indicative pack overlay. Pantry ingredients use the existing policy; Shop prices packs actually purchased. Estimates are unverified.
tip: Pack the paneer and vegetables snugly but do not crush them; a hot grill gives charred edges before the paneer dries out.
method: Mix 150 g yoghurt with one crushed garlic clove, the ginger, cumin, coriander, turmeric, chilli powder, half the lemon juice and 2 g salt. Gently fold in the paneer, pepper and onion. Cover and marinate in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Blend the remaining 100 g yoghurt with the mint leaves, remaining garlic, lemon juice and 1 g salt until a spoonable green chutney forms. Keep chilled until serving.
Heat the grill to high. Thread the marinated paneer and vegetables onto metal skewers, alternating the pieces. Set on a foil-lined tray and brush with all the measured oil.

Grill about 10 cm from the heat for 12–15 minutes, turning every 3–4 minutes, until the vegetables have softened and the paneer edges are golden with a few charred spots. Reposition skewers if one side colours faster.
Warm the pittas for the final 2 minutes under the grill or in a toaster, keeping them clear of raw marinade. Cut into wedges and divide with the skewers between four plates.
Serve the mint chutney alongside. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and use within 48 hours. Reheat paneer and vegetables once until steaming hot; keep the chilled chutney separate.

name: Bombay potatoes
cost_basis: Actual BasketBoss source-aware meal adapter using existing guide packs and the isolated catalogue-700 indicative pack overlay. Pantry ingredients use the existing policy; Shop prices packs actually purchased. Estimates are unverified.
tip: Dry the boiled potatoes briefly in the warm pan before tossing them into the spice base so they hold their shape.
method: Put the potato chunks in a saucepan, cover with cold tap water and add 2 g salt. Bring to the boil and simmer for 10–12 minutes until just tender at the edges but not falling apart.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a wide frying pan. Add the sliced onion and cook over a medium heat for 10 minutes until softened and lightly golden. Stir in the garlic for 1 minute.

Add the cumin, turmeric, ground coriander, chilli powder and remaining salt. Stir for 30 seconds, then add the passata. Simmer for 5 minutes until the tomato mixture is thick and the oil begins to show at the edges.
Drain the potatoes well. Return them to their warm empty saucepan for 1 minute to steam dry, shaking very gently so the chunks keep their shape.
Fold the potatoes into the masala and cook over a medium heat for 5–7 minutes, turning gently, until coated and heated through with a few lightly crisp edges. Add the chopped fresh coriander.
Divide into four side portions; this is an accompaniment rather than a complete dinner. Cool leftovers within 2 hours, refrigerate and use within 48 hours. Reheat once until steaming throughout.

name: Kung pao chicken with rice
cost_basis: Actual BasketBoss source-aware meal adapter using existing guide packs and the isolated catalogue-700 indicative pack overlay. Pantry ingredients use the existing policy; Shop prices packs actually purchased. Estimates are unverified.
tip: The vinegar should remain noticeable against the sweet soy glaze; keep the chicken in small even pieces for quick cooking.
method: Mix the chicken with 15 ml soy sauce and 10 g cornflour. Cover and marinate in the fridge for 15 minutes. Mix the remaining soy sauce and cornflour with the rice vinegar, sugar and 80 ml cold tap water in a small jug.
Cook the rice in 450 ml tap water: bring to the boil, cover and simmer on the lowest heat for 12 minutes, then leave covered off the heat for 8 minutes.
Heat 15 ml oil in a wok until hot. Stir-fry the chicken in two batches for 4–5 minutes per batch until lightly coloured. Transfer to a clean plate between batches.
Add the remaining oil, dried chillies, garlic and ginger and stir for 20 seconds without burning. Add the pepper and spring onions and stir-fry for 2 minutes.

Return the chicken and any juices. Stir the glaze again, pour into the wok and bubble for 2–3 minutes until it coats the chicken. Check the thickest chicken reaches 75°C for 30 seconds; add a splash of water and continue if needed. Fold through the peanuts.

Serve with the fluffed rice, dividing evenly into four portions. The dried chillies are included for flavour but may be left uneaten. Cool rice within 1 hour and refrigerate for up to 24 hours; cool chicken within 2 hours and use within 48 hours. Reheat once until steaming.

cost_basis: Actual BasketBoss source-aware meal adapter using existing guide packs and the isolated catalogue-700 indicative pack overlay. Pantry ingredients use the existing policy; Shop prices packs actually purchased. Estimates are unverified.
tip: Cook the curry sauce gently after adding the cornflour slurry; a short boil removes the chalky taste and gives the familiar takeaway consistency.
method: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the chips with 25 ml oil and the salt. Spread on a large roasting tray in one layer and roast for 30–35 minutes, turning after 20 minutes, until golden and tender.
Meanwhile, heat the remaining 10 ml oil in a large saucepan. Add the onion wedges and cook for 5 minutes until beginning to soften. Add the chicken and stir for 5 minutes until the outside is opaque.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, curry powder and turmeric for 30 seconds. Gradually pour in the stock, scraping the base of the pan, then bring to a gentle simmer.
Simmer uncovered for 10–12 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the thickest piece reaches 75°C for 30 seconds. Add the frozen peas for the final 4 minutes.

Mix the 25 g cornflour with 50 ml cold tap water in a small bowl until completely smooth. Stir the slurry again and pour it into the simmering curry. Divide the hot chips between four plates and spoon over the chicken curry. Cool leftovers within 2 hours, refrigerate and use within 48 hours. Reheat once until steaming throughout; reheat chips separately in a hot oven to regain their texture.

tip: Bake the cases until deeply golden and fill only when ready to eat, so the base stays crisp under the creamy chicken.
method: Heat the oven to 210°C (190°C fan). Cut sixteen 8 cm pastry circles; cut a 5 cm hole from eight circles to make rings. Place whole circles on a lined tray, brush edges with egg and set a ring on each. Save the small centre discs as lids; chill while the oven heats.

Brush the tops with beaten egg without letting it drip down the cut edges. Prick only the central base of each case. Bake the cases and small lids for 18–22 minutes until well risen, deep golden and cooked through.

Meanwhile, melt the butter in a saucepan and cook the onion for 5 minutes. Add the chicken, mushrooms and thyme and cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring, until the mushrooms soften and chicken turns opaque.

Stir in the flour for 1 minute, then gradually add the stock. Simmer for 8–10 minutes until the chicken is cooked through to 75°C for 30 seconds and the sauce is thick. Stir in the cream, salt and pepper and warm for 2 minutes.

Press down or carefully remove any soft pastry from the middle of each cooked case, leaving the crisp base intact. Fill with the hot chicken mixture just before serving and set a small pastry lid on top. Serve two cases per person.

Store leftover filling and pastry separately. Cool filling within 2 hours, refrigerate and use within 48 hours; reheat once until steaming. Keep plain cooled pastry airtight and warm briefly in a hot oven before filling.

name: Homemade malt loaf
cost_basis: Actual BasketBoss source-aware meal adapter using existing guide packs and the isolated catalogue-700 indicative pack overlay. Pantry ingredients use the existing policy; Shop prices packs actually purchased. Estimates are unverified.
tip: Line the loaf tin well and let the loaf cool before slicing. The malt-rich crumb is naturally sticky, but there should be no wet raw batter in the middle.
method: Heat the oven to 170°C (150°C fan). Line a 900 g loaf tin with baking paper, including the sides. Brew the tea bag in 150 ml freshly boiled tap water for 5 minutes, then remove the bag.

Put the brewed tea, malt extract, treacle and sugar in a saucepan and warm gently, stirring, until blended; do not boil vigorously. Add the raisins and sultanas, remove from the heat and leave for 20 minutes, until only lukewarm.

Sift the flour, baking powder and salt into a large bowl. Stir the beaten eggs into the cooled fruit mixture, then fold into the flour until no dry pockets remain. Scrape into the lined tin and level the surface.
Bake for 65–75 minutes until the loaf is firm and a skewer in the centre comes out without wet batter, although sticky fruit may cling to it. Cover loosely with foil if the top darkens too quickly.
Cool in the tin for 15 minutes, then lift onto a rack and cool for a further 30 minutes before cutting. Slice into twelve portions and serve each with 5 g of the listed butter.

Wrap the completely cold loaf and keep in a cool place for up to 3 days, or freeze the slices. For a neater sticky crumb, leave the wrapped cold loaf overnight before slicing; that optional wait is not included in the ready-to-eat timing.

name: Baked eggs in cream with chives
cost_basis: Actual BasketBoss source-aware meal adapter using existing guide packs and the isolated catalogue-700 indicative pack overlay. Pantry ingredients use the existing policy; Shop prices packs actually purchased. Estimates are unverified.
tip: The water bath protects the eggs from fierce heat. Take the ramekins out carefully as soon as the whites set, and keep the handles or rims away from children.
method: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Butter four heatproof ramekins of roughly 250 ml capacity and stand them in a deep roasting tin. Boil a kettle of tap water for the water bath.

Pour 20 ml cream into each ramekin and crack in two eggs without breaking the yolks. Add the remaining 20 ml cream per ramekin, season lightly with the salt and pepper, and scatter with half the chives.

Set the tin on an oven shelf, then carefully pour hot tap water into the tin to reach halfway up the ramekin sides. Keep water out of the eggs. Bake for 18–25 minutes until the whites are fully set; the exact time depends on the depth of the ramekins.

For anyone needing fully cooked eggs, continue until the yolks are set as well. Toast the bread during the last few minutes. Lift the hot ramekins out with a cloth or suitable tongs and set each on a heatproof plate.
Scatter with the remaining chives and serve immediately with one toast slice per person. Warn diners that the ramekins are hot. This recipe serves four people, with two eggs each.

Prepare only the portions wanted and keep unused eggs and cream chilled according to their labels. The soft texture is best fresh; do not leave baked eggs standing at room temperature or repeatedly reheat them.

Cook the parcels seam-side down for 3–4 minutes, pressing gently, then turn and cook for 2–3 minutes until golden and sealed. Cook in two batches if needed. Halve and serve immediately so the central corn tortilla stays crunchy.

name: Beef bourguignon with mash
category: Date Nights · Special meals for two
cost_basis: Actual BasketBoss source-aware meal adapter using existing guide packs and the isolated catalogue-700 indicative pack overlay. Pantry ingredients use the existing policy; Shop prices packs actually purchased. Estimates are unverified.
tip: Low, gentle braising turns economical beef into tender pieces; red wine supplies the defining sauce.
method: Heat the oven to 150°C (130°C fan). Fry the bacon in a lidded casserole until its fat renders, then lift out. Add the oil and brown the dry beef in batches; do not crowd the pan. Set the meat aside and soften the onions and carrots in the same pan for 8 minutes.

Stir in the garlic for 1 minute, return the beef and bacon and sprinkle over the flour. Stir for 1 minute. Gradually pour in the wine and stock, scraping the browned base. Add the thyme, bay, 2 g salt and pepper. Bring to a simmer, cover tightly and braise in the oven for 3 hours until the beef yields easily to a fork.

Add the mushrooms for the final 30 minutes of braising. If the beef is still firm, continue in 20-minute intervals. When tender, lift out the thyme and bay. Simmer uncovered on the hob for 10 minutes if the sauce needs reducing; avoid a fierce boil that toughens the meat.

During the final 25 minutes, boil the potatoes in tap water until very tender, then drain and steam dry for 2 minutes. Mash with the warm milk, butter and remaining 2 g salt. Serve four portions of bourguignon over mash. Cool leftovers promptly, refrigerate within 2 hours and reheat once until steaming hot within 48 hours.

name: Hunter’s chicken with chips
cost_basis: Actual BasketBoss source-aware meal adapter using existing guide packs and the isolated catalogue-700 indicative pack overlay. Pantry ingredients use the existing policy; Shop prices packs actually purchased. Estimates are unverified.
tip: Use similar-sized chicken breasts and check their centres, since bubbling cheese alone does not show that the chicken is cooked.
method: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Dry the chips, toss with 25 ml oil, measured salt, paprika and half the pepper, and spread on a large roasting tray. Roast for 35–40 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and tender.

Grease a separate shallow baking dish with the remaining 5 ml oil. Season the chicken with the remaining pepper and wrap each breast with two thin bacon rashers, keeping the bacon seam underneath. Wash hands, boards and utensils after handling raw chicken.

Put the wrapped chicken in the oven after the chips have cooked for about 10 minutes. Bake for 20 minutes, then spoon 50 ml BBQ sauce over each breast and divide the grated Cheddar evenly over the top.

Return to the oven for 8–12 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and the thickest chicken reaches 75°C for 30 seconds. Check the meat with a clean probe rather than measuring only the hot cheese. If necessary, loosely cover the cheese and continue cooking until the chicken is safe.

Rest the chicken for 3–5 minutes, then serve one bacon-wrapped, BBQ-and-Cheddar-topped breast per person with a quarter of the chips and its dish juices. This pub-style version uses unbreaded chicken.

Cool cooked leftovers within 2 hours, refrigerate and use within 48 hours, or freeze promptly. Defrost in the fridge and reheat once until steaming hot throughout; cook only the portions of chips you want to eat immediately for the best texture.

name: Bacon and onion suet roly-poly
cost_basis: Actual BasketBoss source-aware meal adapter using existing guide packs and the isolated catalogue-700 indicative pack overlay. Pantry ingredients use the existing policy; Shop prices packs actually purchased. Estimates are unverified.
tip: Let the filling cool before rolling and leave expansion room inside the wrapper so the suet pastry stays light.
method: Heat the oil in a frying pan and soften the onion for 8 minutes. Add the chopped bacon and cook for 7–9 minutes until cooked through to 75°C for 30 seconds. Stir in the parsley and half the pepper, then spread on a plate to cool.

Mix 285 g flour with the suet, salt and remaining pepper. Stir in 150–170 ml cold tap water gradually to make a soft but not sticky dough. Dust a work surface with the reserved flour and roll the dough into a rectangle about 28 x 35 cm.

Spread the cooled filling over the dough, leaving a 2 cm border. Roll up from one long edge and pinch the seam and ends closed. Set on butter-free baking paper, then wrap loosely in a double sheet of foil with room for the dough to expand; fold the ends securely.

Put a trivet in a large lidded saucepan and add boiling tap water to just below it. Set the wrapped roll on the trivet, cover and steam gently for 2 hours. Check every 25–30 minutes and top up with boiling water so the pan never boils dry.

Lift out carefully, rest for 10 minutes and unwrap away from your face because steam will escape. The dough must be cooked through with no sticky raw centre and the filling piping hot. Slice into eight thick pieces and serve two slices per person.

Refrigerate leftover slices within 2 hours and use within 48 hours. Reheat once by steaming until piping hot throughout. The recipe uses tap water in the dough and steaming pan; it adds no gravy or side dish to the shopping list.

tip: Dry sausages and a light flour dusting help thick cornmeal batter cling evenly.

tip: Freeze banana in a single layer so the slices blend easily; keep the mixture thick enough to eat with a spoon.
method: Peel two bananas, cut into thick slices and arrange on a small lined tray. Freeze for at least 4 hours until solid. This advance freezing time is included in the recipe time; if using bananas you have already frozen, begin with the next step.

name: Baked ricotta with roasted plums
cost_basis: Actual BasketBoss source-aware meal adapter using existing guide packs and the isolated catalogue-700 indicative pack overlay. Pantry ingredients use the existing policy; Shop prices packs actually purchased. Estimates are unverified.
tip: Drain wet ricotta first so the baked pots set softly rather than turning watery.
method: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Grease four small ovenproof ramekins with the butter and set on a baking tray. Drain excess liquid from the ricotta.
Whisk ricotta with eggs, 30 g honey, vanilla and finely grated lemon zest until evenly combined. Divide between the ramekins and smooth the tops without packing tightly.
Halve and stone the plums. Put cut-side up in a small baking dish, drizzle with the remaining 20 g honey and 20 ml lemon juice, and place in the oven alongside the ramekins.

Bake the ricotta for 25–30 minutes until lightly golden at the edges and set in the centre, reaching 75°C for 30 seconds. Roast plums for about 20–25 minutes until tender and juicy, removing sooner if they soften quickly.

Rest the ricotta for 5 minutes. Serve one ramekin per person with three plum halves and their roasting juices. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and use within 48 hours; reheat once until steaming or eat chilled if properly stored.

name: Cinnamon baked apples with cottage cheese and pecans
cost_basis: Actual BasketBoss source-aware meal adapter using existing guide packs and the isolated catalogue-700 indicative pack overlay. Pantry ingredients use the existing policy; Shop prices packs actually purchased. Estimates are unverified.
tip: Keep the apple base intact and score the skin lightly so the nut filling stays in place while it bakes.
method: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Wash and core the apples carefully, leaving a little flesh at the base to hold the filling. Score a shallow line around the skin of each apple so it can expand without bursting.
Mix 20 g chopped pecans with cinnamon and 15 g honey. Put 5 g butter in each apple cavity, divide the nut mixture between them and set in a small baking dish. Add 50 ml tap water around the apples.

Bake for 30–40 minutes, basting once with the dish juices, until the apples are tender when pierced but still hold their shape. The exact time depends on size and variety. Rest for 5 minutes before handling.
Put each warm apple in a shallow bowl, open the cavity a little and add 100 g chilled cottage cheese, spooning any excess alongside. Finish with the remaining pecans and honey divided equally.

Serve promptly. Refrigerate leftover baked apples within 2 hours and use within 48 hours; store cottage cheese separately according to its pack use-by date. Reheat apple once before adding fresh cold cottage cheese.

name: Dutch baby with lemon and blueberries
cost_basis: Actual BasketBoss source-aware meal adapter using existing guide packs and the isolated catalogue-700 indicative pack overlay. Pantry ingredients use the existing policy; Shop prices packs actually purchased. Estimates are unverified.
tip: A properly heated pan and immediate pouring give the oven pancake its tall, crisp-edged puff.
method: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) with a 22–24 cm ovenproof heavy frying pan inside. Make sure the pan has no plastic parts and its handle is safe at this temperature.
Whisk eggs, milk, flour, caster sugar and finely grated lemon zest until smooth. Let the batter stand while the oven and pan heat, about 10 minutes. Wash and dry the blueberries.

Using oven gloves, take out the hot pan, add the butter and swirl to coat the base and sides. Pour in the batter immediately and return to the oven. Bake for 20–25 minutes without opening the door early, until dramatically puffed with golden edges and a set centre.

Remove carefully; the handle stays very hot. Scatter with blueberries, dust with the measured icing sugar and squeeze over lemon juice to taste. Cut into two generous portions and serve immediately as it naturally deflates.
Do not add raw blueberries to the batter for this version. Refrigerate any leftovers within 2 hours and use within 48 hours, reheating once until steaming; the puffed texture is best fresh.

tip: Loosen the segments before baking so warm grapefruit can be eaten neatly with a spoon.
method: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Halve the grapefruits through the equator, remove seeds and loosen the segments with a small knife, keeping the halves intact.
Set cut-side up in a small baking dish. Divide the honey equally between the four halves and sprinkle lightly with the measured nutmeg.
